nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking improvement needed in the FP32 test tolerances.

Findings

1.  **FP32 checks miss lost precision** ▶

Summary

Enables FP16 and FP32 expert-parallel payloads alongside BF16. - PyTorch EP carries payloads in the dtype chosen for each buffer. - JAX EP accepts token dtypes within the group's bootstrap limit. Reviews (7) · Last reviewed commit: ["Check payload width in EP combine and di..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/e0a9329b5c2f79ac2889ba892d633ed7deb437c9) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Bootstrap dtype mismatch** This check only verifies that the tensor matches `buffer.payload_dtype`; it does not verify that the payload fits the group's bootstrap-time `max_token_dtype`. For example, the default BF16 bootstrap and an FP32 `EpBuffer` pass this check, but native dispatch rejects the wider payload while combine has no equivalent width check before forwarding it to NCCL EP. Validating the buffer dtype against the bootstrap maximum would reject this inconsistent configuration before communication starts. **Knowledge Base Used:** [PyTorch distributed execution](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/pytorch-distributed-execution.md)

We're seeing a test failure in this test:
```
ERROR: test_primitive_dispatch_combine_identity_dtypes (__main__.TestEP.test_primitive_dispatch_combine_identity_dtypes) (dtype=<class 'jax.numpy.float32'>)
Round-robin identity round-trip for each high-precision payload dtype
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/transformerengine/tests/jax/test_multi_process_ep.py", line 529, in test_primitive_dispatch_combine_identity_dtypes
    self._run_identity_round_trip(nonuniform=False, dtype=dt)
  File "/opt/transformerengine/tests/jax/test_multi_process_ep.py", line 503, in _run_identity_round_trip
    out.block_until_ready()
jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError: UNKNOWN: XLA FFI call failed: /opt/transformerengine/transformer_engine/common/ep/ep_backend.cpp:506 in function dispatch: Assertion failed: typeToSize(static_cast<DType>(tok_dtype)) <= typeToSize(static_cast<DType>(group_config_.max_token_dtype)). tokens dtype (4) wider than group max_token_dtype (6) [executable_name='jit_run']
```
I see that we call `ep_bootstrap` with `max_token_dtype=jnp.float32`, but it seems that NCCP EP is still being initialized with BF16.

**EP buffer tests fail immediately** `_make_buffer()` now always passes `payload_dtype` to `_make_config()`, but `_make_config()` accepts neither that argument nor `**kwargs`. Every test using `_make_buffer()` therefore raises `TypeError` before dispatch, including existing BF16 tests and the new dtype sweep. Add the argument to `_make_config()` and pass it into `EpConfig` so the requested dtype reaches the buffer.

nodes.body: **FP32 checks miss lost precision** The new FP32 round-trip and gradient checks use `atol=5e-2, rtol=5e-2` on inputs near 0.1–0.9. A payload rounded to BF16 and then returned as FP32 passes both numeric checks and the dtype assertions, so this test can miss lost FP32 precision in either direction. Use dtype-specific tolerances with a tight FP32 threshold. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

inline_comments.body: **Bootstrap dtype mismatch** This check only verifies that the tensor matches `buffer.payload_dtype`; it does not verify that the payload fits the group's bootstrap-time `max_token_dtype`. For example, the default BF16 bootstrap and an FP32 `EpBuffer` pass this check, but native dispatch rejects the wider payload while combine has no equivalent width check before forwarding it to NCCL EP. Validating the buffer dtype against the bootstrap maximum would reject this inconsistent configuration before communication starts. **Knowledge Base Used:** [PyTorch distributed execution](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/pytorch-distributed-execution.md)

inline_comments.body: **FP32 checks miss lost precision** The new FP32 round-trip and gradient checks use `atol=5e-2, rtol=5e-2` on inputs near 0.1–0.9. A payload rounded to BF16 and then returned as FP32 passes both numeric checks and the dtype assertions, so this test can miss lost FP32 precision in either direction. Use dtype-specific tolerances with a tight FP32 threshold. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!
